content.comment_body: For [product_name] models, certain switching limitations apply depending on the type of load: resistive loads are allowed up to 10A, while inductive loads are allowed up to 3A. It is known that LED lights may have inrush currents that can reach up to 100 times the continuous rating of the LED driver's specification. When using [product_name] to switch LED or SMD lights, what is the maximum switching capacity for the relay contacts, and how much could frequent high inrush currents impact their service life?
Please review the information on the [company_name] website regarding the inrush current limiter [product_name], as it may offer relevant guidance.

analysis.insight_summary: The user is requesting information about the operational limits of [product_name]'s relay contacts when used to control LED or SMD lighting, particularly in relation to the high inrush currents typical of such devices. The conversation points out concerns about the impact on relay lifespan and seeks more detailed advice or documentation to safely handle high inrush loads with the hardware.
analysis.user_expectations: The user expects to receive clear recommendations on relay switching capacities for LED loads, along with practical advice regarding the effect of inrush currents on contact lifespan when operating [product_name] in these scenarios.
